mapmc-pmc-2022-11-p2.title: Check each shape
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-p2.body:
The shapes are a triangle, a long rectangle, a slanted parallelogram, a square and another slanted parallelogram. A square needs four equal sides **and** four right angles, so only the fourth shape is a square.

**Answer: (A) 1**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-p2.title: Rule out the look-alikes
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-p2.body:
The rectangle has right angles but two sides are longer. The parallelograms have equal-looking sides in places but no right angles. That leaves just one square.

**Answer: (A) 1**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-01.title: Use the biggest coins first
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-01.body:
Take the biggest coin that fits: 5p (3p left), then 2p (1p left), then 1p. That is 3 coins: $5 + 2 + 1 = 8$.

**Answer: (A) 3**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-01.title: Why not 2 coins?
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-01.body:
Two UK coins can make 2p, 3p, 4p, 6p, 7p, 10p, … but never 8p (there is no 3p, 4p or 6p coin to pair with another). So 3 coins is the smallest.

**Answer: (A) 3**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-02.title: Scale up
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-02.body:
100 miles is $4 \times 25$ miles, so it needs 4 charges: $4 \times 20\text{p} = 80\text{p}$.

**Answer: (A) 80p**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-02.title: Cost per mile
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-02.body:
20p for 25 miles is $\frac{20}{25} = 0.8$p per mile, so 100 miles costs 80p.

**Answer: (A) 80p**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-03.title: Count the cats
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-03.body:
Tilly plus 4 kittens is 5 cats. $5 \times 3 = 15$ treats.

**Answer: (C) 15**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-04.title: Half a turn
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-04.body:
180° is half a turn, which always points you in the opposite direction. The opposite of east is west.

**Answer: (E) west**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-04.title: Two quarter turns
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-04.body:
Clockwise from east: a quarter turn (90°) takes him to south, another quarter turn takes him to west.

**Answer: (E) west**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-05.title: How far in an hour
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-05.body:
An hour is 3 lots of 20 minutes, so in an hour she would cycle 3 miles: 3 mph.

**Answer: (B) 3 mph**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-05.title: Speed = distance ÷ time
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-05.body:
20 minutes is $\frac13$ of an hour. $1 \div \frac13 = 3$ miles per hour.

**Answer: (B) 3 mph**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-06.title: Draw the triangles
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-06.body:
The base of the sphinx is 3 triangle-sides long. Along the bottom row fit 3 upward and 2 downward triangles (5 in all), and the head on top is 1 more triangle: 6.

**Answer: (C) 6**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-06.title: Compare areas
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-06.body:
The head is one small triangle. The body is a trapezium which is a triangle of side 3 (9 small triangles) with the top part (a triangle of side 2, 4 small triangles) cut off: $9 - 4 = 5$. Total $5 + 1 = 6$.

**Answer: (C) 6**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-07.title: Group the animals
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-07.body:
One parrot, one cat and one dog have $2 + 4 + 4 = 10$ legs. 30 legs means 3 such groups, so there are 3 cats.

**Answer: (B) 3**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-07.title: Check an option
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-07.body:
With 3 of each: parrots $3 \times 2 = 6$, cats $3 \times 4 = 12$, dogs $3 \times 4 = 12$. $6 + 12 + 12 = 30$ ✓.

**Answer: (B) 3**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-08.title: Closing speed
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-08.body:
Each second the gap shrinks by $7 + 4 = 11$ cm. $44 \div 11 = 4$ seconds.

**Answer: (C) 4 sec**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-08.title: Second by second
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-08.body:
Gap: 44 → 33 → 22 → 11 → 0 cm. That is 4 seconds.

**Answer: (C) 4 sec**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-09.title: Days per pair
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-09.body:
Each pair lasts 3 days, and he has 9 pairs: $9 \times 3 = 27$ days.

**Answer: (D) 27**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-09.title: Careful with socks vs pairs
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-09.body:
He wears 2 socks at a time, so the 18 socks give 9 changes. $9 \times 3 = 27$ days (not $18 \times 3$).

**Answer: (D) 27**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-10.title: Two sides per triangle
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-10.body:
Each triangle has its base on the dotted line and its other two sides on the zigzag. In an equilateral triangle those two sides together are twice the base. The bases add up to the dotted line, 12 cm, so the zigzag is $2 \times 12 = 24$ cm.

**Answer: (D) 24 cm**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-10.title: Imagine equal triangles
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-10.body:
The answer does not depend on the sizes, so pretend there are 4 equal triangles each with a base of 3 cm. Each adds $3 + 3 = 6$ cm of zigzag: $4 \times 6 = 24$ cm.

**Answer: (D) 24 cm**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-11.title: Same price, most packets
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-11.body:
Every offer costs the price of 2 packets. The best one gives the most packets for that money: 5 for the price of 2.

**Answer: (E) 5 for the price of 2**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-11.title: Price per packet
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-11.body:
If one packet normally costs £1, the offers cost per packet: £2, £1, about 67p, 50p and 40p. The cheapest is 40p.

**Answer: (E) 5 for the price of 2**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-12.title: Clear the exit row
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-12.body:
The car park is 4 squares wide and 5 deep, and my car is in the middle row on the left. Two upright cars block my row: one in the third column and one in the fourth (next to the exit). Each must leave the middle row completely.
- **Fourth-column car:** above it is another upright car stuck against the top wall, so it must go down one square. That square is taken by the flat car on the bottom row, so first slide the bottom flat car one square left (it can move only that far). Then move the fourth-column car down. (2 cars)
- **Third-column car:** it cannot go down, since the bottom flat car still covers the third column wherever it can be. So it must go up two squares, and those squares are covered by the two flat cars in the top two rows. Slide both of those left one square, then move the third-column car up to the top wall. (3 cars)

That is $2 + 3 = 5$ cars, and each of these moves was forced, so fewer is impossible.

**Answer: (C) 5**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-13.title: Go year by year
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-13.body:
2023 to 2029 have digit totals 7 to 13. 2030 totals 5 and 2031 totals 6. $2031 - 2022 = 9$ years.

**Answer: (D) 9**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-13.title: Think about the last two digits
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-13.body:
In 20__, the first two digits give 2, so the last two digits must total 4. After 22 the next two-digit number with digits adding to 4 is 31. $31 - 22 = 9$.

**Answer: (D) 9**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-14.title: Count up
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-14.body:
1 bar: 7.5 g, 2 bars: 15 g, 3 bars: 22.5 g, 4 bars: 30 g (too much). So at most 3.

**Answer: (C) 3**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-14.title: Divide
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-14.body:
$24 \div 7.5 = 3.2$, so 3 whole bars fit within the limit.

**Answer: (C) 3**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-15.title: Cost for a whole year
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-15.body:
- £50 for 6 months: $2 \times 50 = £100$
- £26 for 3 months: $4 \times 26 = £104$
- £18 for 2 months: $6 \times 18 = £108$
- annual: £120
- £9 a month: $12 \times 9 = £108$

**Answer: (A) £50 for 6 months**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-15.title: Cost per month
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-15.body:
Per month: A $50 \div 6 \approx £8.33$, B $26 \div 3 \approx £8.67$, C £9, D £10, E £9. A is cheapest.

**Answer: (A) £50 for 6 months**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-16.title: Find the distance
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-16.body:
At 50 mph for 3 hours the journey is $50 \times 3 = 150$ miles. At 150 mph that takes 1 hour.

**Answer: (D) 1 hour**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-16.title: Three times as fast
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-16.body:
150 mph is 3 times as fast as 50 mph, so it takes a third of the time: $3 \div 3 = 1$ hour.

**Answer: (D) 1 hour**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-17.title: Multiple of 4 and 5
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-17.body:
The number must be a multiple of 5, so it ends in 0 or 5. Only 120 does, and $120 = 4 \times 30$ too.

**Answer: (E) 120**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-17.title: Multiple of 20
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-17.body:
Multiples of both 4 and 5 are multiples of 20: 20, 40, …, 100, 120. Only 120 is in the list.

**Answer: (E) 120**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-18.title: Find all the sides
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-18.body:
Top room: $42 \div 6 = 7$ m long. Bottom room: $20 \div 4 = 5$ m long. The bottom room starts 4 m from the left edge, so it reaches $4 + 5 = 9$ m, which is 2 m past the top room. Going clockwise from the top-left corner: $7 + 6 + 2 + 4 + 5 + 4 + 4 + 6 = 38$ m (top, right of top room, step across, right of bottom room, bottom, left of bottom room, the 4 m step back, left of top room).

**Answer: (B) 38 m**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-18.title: Use the surrounding rectangle
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-18.body:
The shape is a staircase, so its perimeter equals the perimeter of the rectangle around it. That rectangle is $4 + 5 = 9$ m wide and $6 + 4 = 10$ m tall: $2 \times (9 + 10) = 38$ m.

**Answer: (B) 38 m**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-19.title: Simplify each fraction
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-19.body:
$999999999 = 3 \times 333333333$, so the first fraction is $\frac13$. Similarly $\frac{444444444}{888888888} = \frac12$ and $\frac{111111111}{666666666} = \frac16$. Then $\frac13 + \frac12 + \frac16 = \frac26 + \frac36 + \frac16 = \frac66 = 1$.

**Answer: (D) 1**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-19.title: Think of digits
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-19.body:
Each fraction is the same as its one-digit version: $\frac39 + \frac48 + \frac16$ (divide top and bottom by 111111111). That is $\frac13 + \frac12 + \frac16 = 1$.

**Answer: (D) 1**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-20.title: Round first
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-20.body:
37.36 seconds rounds to 37 (0.36 is less than a half). $24 \times 60 + 37 = 1440 + 37 = 1477$.

**Answer: (D) 1477**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-21.title: Rectangle minus three triangles
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-21.body:
The rectangle is 15 cm by 8 cm, area 120 cm². The three white right-angled triangles:
- top right: $\frac12 \times 8 \times 8 = 32$ cm²
- top left: legs 5 cm and $15 - 8 = 7$ cm: $\frac12 \times 5 \times 7 = 17.5$ cm²
- bottom: legs 15 cm and $8 - 5 = 3$ cm: $\frac12 \times 15 \times 3 = 22.5$ cm²

Shaded: $120 - 32 - 17.5 - 22.5 = 48$ cm².

**Answer: 48 cm²**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-21.title: Use coordinates
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-21.body:
Put the bottom-left corner of the rectangle at $(0, 0)$. The triangle's corners are $(0, 3)$ (5 cm down from the top), $(7, 8)$ (8 cm from the right on the top edge) and $(15, 0)$. Draw the vertical line $x = 7$ through the top corner: it splits the shaded triangle into two triangles sharing that line. The slanting bottom side crosses $x = 7$ at height $3 - 3 \times \frac{7}{15} = 1.6$, so the shared side is $8 - 1.6 = 6.4$ cm. The two parts have widths 7 and 8, so the area is $\frac12 \times 6.4 \times (7 + 8) = 48$ cm².

**Answer: 48 cm²**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-22.title: Long pieces and short pieces
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-22.body:
Across the frame there are 3 strips of wood (top, middle, bottom) and 2 photos, so each horizontal piece is $3 \times 2 + 2 \times 15 = 36$ cm long: $3 \times 36 = 108$ cm. Between them, in each of the 2 rows of photos, there are 3 upright pieces each 15 cm long: $6 \times 15 = 90$ cm. Total $108 + 90 = 198$ cm.

**Answer: 198 cm**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-22.title: Use area
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-22.body:
The frame is a $36 \times 36$ square with four $15 \times 15$ holes, so the wood covers $1296 - 4 \times 225 = 396$ cm². The wood is 2 cm wide, so its length is $396 \div 2 = 198$ cm.

**Answer: 198 cm**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-23.title: Imagine 100 children
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-23.body:
With 100 children, 75 like netball. 60% of 75 is $\frac{6}{10} \times 75 = 45$ children, which is 45% of the class.

**Answer: 45%**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-24.title: Angles around a point
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-24.body:
Each angle of a regular pentagon is $\frac{(5-2) \times 180°}{5} = 108°$. At each gap, three pentagons (the middle one and two outer ones) meet at a point, and the angles round a point make 360°. So the gap is $360° - 3 \times 108° = 36°$.

**Answer: 36°**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-24.title: Walk round the pentagon
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-24.body:
Walking round a pentagon you turn 5 times to make a full 360° turn, so each turn is 72° and each inside angle is $180° - 72° = 108°$. Then the gap is $360° - 324° = 36°$.

**Answer: 36°**

mapmc-pmc-2022-11-25.title: Use the symmetry
mapmc-pmc-2022-11-25.body:
Turn the whole picture half a turn about the centre of the rectangle. The diagonal $BD$ lands on itself, the two circles swap places, and the part above the diagonal swaps with the part below. Under this turn every shaded piece lands exactly on an unshaded piece of the same size, and the other way round. So exactly half of the rectangle is shaded: $\frac12 \times 14 \times 7 = 49$ cm².

**Answer: 49 cm²**
